lede: From the Decree of Kutná Hora to the battle of Vítkov. Stations say what modern accounts agree on; as the modules are carried, each station is linked to the passage that tells it.

stations.text: King Wenceslas IV gives the Bohemian nation three votes and the foreign nations one at the university of Prague; the German masters and students leave for Leipzig. Hus becomes rector. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Archbishop Zbyněk has Wyclif's books burned in Prague; Hus, who goes on preaching at the Bethlehem Chapel, is excommunicated. (Modern accounts; module planned.)

Hus attacks the indulgences sold for John XXIII's war against Naples; three young men who contradict the preachers are beheaded. Hus is placed under a heavier excommunication and leaves Prague for the countryside. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
In exile Hus writes his treatise on the Church, and preaches in Czech to the people of southern Bohemia. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
At Speyer, Sigismund's chancery issues the letter that takes Hus 'into our protection and that of the holy empire', with free passage to Constance and back.
The Council of Constance opens under John XXIII. Hus arrives on 3 November with Sigismund's safe conduct; on 28 November two bishops come to his lodging, and he does not come back.
John XXIII escapes from Constance in disguise; the council declares itself above the pope (Haec sancta, 6 April) and later deposes him. (Modern accounts; module planned.)

Four days after the pope's flight, Hus's gaolers leave with their master. He writes to Chlum: 'If you love your poor Goose, get the King to send me guards from his own court or to set me free.' The king hands him to the bishop of Constance instead.

Hus is heard three times before the council in the Franciscan refectory. On 7 June Sigismund defends his safe conduct to Hus's face; on 8 June, thinking Hus's friends have gone, he tells the council not to believe a recantation.
Expecting to die the next day, Hus writes to the two noblemen who brought him to Constance: God 'deceives no man by a safe-conduct'; 'Sigismund hath acted deceitfully throughout.'

The council condemns Hus as a heretic in the cathedral, degrades him from the priesthood and gives him to the secular arm; he is burned the same day outside the walls, and his ashes are thrown into the Rhine.
Lords of Bohemia and Moravia seal a letter of protest to the council. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Hus's friend Jerome, who had recanted and withdrawn his recantation, is burned at Constance. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
The council elects Martin V; the great schism is over. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
After a procession led by the preacher Jan Želivský, councillors of the New Town of Prague are thrown from the town hall windows. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
King Wenceslas IV dies; the heir is his brother Sigismund. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Radicals found Tábor in southern Bohemia; the pope proclaims a crusade against the heretics of Bohemia, and Jan Žižka's wagons hold at Sudoměř. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Žižka's men hold the hill of Vítkov above Prague against Sigismund's crusading army. (Modern accounts; module planned.)

stations.titel: A king crowned in a castle
stations.text: Sigismund has himself crowned king of Bohemia in the cathedral of Prague castle, while the city below holds against him. The Four Articles of Prague are proclaimed that summer: the free preaching of the word, the chalice for the laity, a Church without worldly property, and the punishment of mortal sins. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
